newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti, Consob to issue statement on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti, Consob to issue statement on Friday.

text.p: Italy's troubled hi-tech company Olivetti is set to issue a statement on Friday morning after the money-losing group met with stock market watchdog Consob on Thursday aimed at clarifying its financial accounts.

An Olivetti spokeswoman said after the 3-1/2 hour meeting in Rome between Consob and Olivetti officials led by Chief Executive Francesco Caio that there would be a joint Olivetti-Consob communique issued on Friday morning.

Earlier on Thursday, Consob met with Renzo Francesconi, a former Olivetti director-general who resigned on Wednesday after only six week at the company, when he expressed misgivings about the way Olivetti presented its first half 1996 results.
"We gave all the elements to Consob to show Francesconi's statements were groundless," Caio told reporters after the meeting with Consob had finished.
Olivetti shares were suspended on the Milan stock exchange ahead of the meetings called by Consob, and were likely to remain suspended until the statement on Friday morning.

This was the latest twist in a week of high drama which had seen Olivetti's stock price plunge and then stabilise after tycoon Carlo De Benedetti resigned as chairman on Tuesday, ending 18 years at the helm.

Caio, widely seen as having won out in a boardroom power struggle with De Benedetti, had been summoned to Rome by Consob along with De Benedetti's successor as Chairman Antonio Tesone and other company officials.
Olivetti said on Thursday that Francesconi's comments were completely unfounded and that it had instructed lawyers "to take action in defence of the company's moral standing."
